newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures alike, were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Carryover strength in live cattle futures was expected to follow higher boxed beef prices Thursday and active feedlot cattle sales this week at higher prices. Packers continued to buy cattle Friday after brisk sales earlier in the week, which points to their need for slaughter supplies and likely continued good beef demand, analysts said.
However, scale up commercial hedge selling is expected to continue, they said.
Fed cattle supplies will be increasing the next couple of months based on active feedlot placements earlier in the year, sources noted.

Feeder cattle futures were also expected to show carryover demand after posting new contract highs and highest levels since January 1995. Active feedlot marketings and good grazing conditions has kept demand for feeders strong, analysts said.
However, corn futures could influence trade, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.17 at $72.32 per cwt.
